title: Mini-slot affinity and timeout heuristics — experiment notes
content:
Status: working notes / draft for postmort and follow-ups.

Summary
- Goal: reduce 99.9th/99th token latency spikes on mixed workloads (small chat vs long-completion) without regressing p50/p95 and while keeping average GPU utilization >= 65%.
- Idea: introduce "mini-slot" concept (micro-batches that prefer requests with KV-cache affinity) + a soft timeout hysteresis that delays flush for a few ms if an affinity-compatible request is likely to arrive.
- Motivation: observed tail spikes when a long-open KV context is followed by many short requests that cannot reuse KV cache leading to many cold KV loads and kernel thrash. Current coalescing too coarse: either waits for full batch (adds latency) or flushes too often (wastes kernels).

Experiment design
- Environment: ded-testpool-6 (A100s), CUDA 12.2, runtime commit 6f12b9d (branch: mini-slot-experiments).
- Workloads: 3 synthetic mixes plus a replay of production traces from 2025-10-12 (channel: product-chat).
- Metrics captured: per-token latency histogram, request end-to-end (E2E), GPU kernel occupancy, KV cache hit ratio, batching delay, per-queue length, fairness index (Jain), tail QPS drop events.
- Baseline: current hybrid-window coalescer (stable), baseline p99 token time: 220ms, p999 token time: 420ms, avg GPU util 72%, KV hit ratio 48% on trace.

Parameter grid (parallel runs)
- mini_slot_size: [4, 8, 16] requests
- affinity_window_ms: [8, 16, 32]
- soft_hysteresis_ms: [2, 5, 10]
- prefill_threshold_pct (how full a mini-slot must be to skip waiting): [50, 75, 100]
- max_wait_ms (hard cap): [40, 80]
Total combinations sampled ~ 3*3*3*3*2 = 162 runs (short runs for initial sweep).

Quick notes on the algorithm
- Requests are assigned a score: affinity_score = KV_cache_age_penalty + same-model-tag_bonus + route_priority_bonus.
- Mini-slots are logical buckets sized by mini_slot_size; scheduler attempts to fill a mini-slot with high-affinity requests first to maximize KV reuse.
- soft_hysteresis_ms delays flush of a not-yet-full mini-slot if an incoming request of higher affinity is predicted in next soft_hysteresis_ms based on short-term arrival estimator (EWMA).
- If prefill_threshold_pct is reached, the mini-slot flushes immediately even if soft_hysteresis_ms still counting.

Representative results (selected runs)
- Run A (mini_slot_size=8, affinity_window_ms=16, soft_hysteresis_ms=5, prefill=75, max_wait=80):
  - p50 token: 18ms (no change), p95: 42ms (slightly better), p99: 160ms (improved from 220ms), p999: 280ms (improved from 420ms).
  - GPU util: 69% (safe), KV hit ratio: 61% (+13ppt).
  - Notes: fewer kernel cold-starts on trace segments with repeated chat contexts.}
  
- Run B (mini_slot_size=4, affinity_window_ms=8, soft_hysteresis_ms=2, prefill=50, max_wait=40):
  - p50 token: 20ms, p95: 46ms, p99: 210ms (small improvement), p999: 400ms (almost baseline).
  - GPU util: 74% (a little higher), KV hit ratio: 53% (+5ppt).
  - Notes: lighter hysteresis avoids holding short requests too long; still some tail events where small bursts of unrelated requests preempt affinity filling.

- Run C (mini_slot_size=16, affinity_window_ms=32, soft_hysteresis_ms=10, prefill=100, max_wait=80):
  - p50: 21ms, p95: 58ms (regression), p99: 310ms (worse), p999: 520ms (worse).
  - GPU util: 64% (dropped), KV hit ratio: 70% (+22ppt)
  - Notes: aggressive affinity waiting formed large coalesced batches but increased per-request batching delay for short requests; not acceptable for PLG latency SLOs.

Profiling observations
- Flame graphs (kernel-level) show the following patterns for improved runs (A): less time spent in kernel init paths and memcpy-to-GPU per token; more time in decode kernels as expected.
- Hot spots before change: heavy spikes in LRU eviction + KV deserialization when many unrelated requests caused parallel KV loads. After mini-slot affinity, KV deserialization spikes were smoothed.
- CPU-side: scheduler lock contention dropped by ~30% on improved runs (we moved to per-mini-slot non-blocking queues).

Fairness tradeoffs and metrics
- Introduced fairness_index (Jain) on per-route throughput across 60s windows. Baseline fairness ~0.88. Run A fairness ~0.84 (slight demotion of very-low-priority routes), Run B fairness ~0.87.
- Observed a class of starvation for ephemeral low-priority requests on very bursty long-request traffic when prefill=100 and large mini_slot_size — mitigated by adding a per-slot age-based demotion after age_threshold_ms.

Concrete failure / edge case found
- Under heavy heterogeneous arrival (mix of very short API pings and occasional long context completions), mini-slot affinity caused a rare pathological case where a slot waited for affinity matches while many unrelated short requests timed out and retried, causing a spike of retries and increased load (cascading). Reproducible in replay when RTT jitter > 60ms between clients.
- Mitigation: enforce max_wait_ms hard cap and detect retry trains by monitoring identical request signatures within 500ms; in presence of retries, short-circuit affinity wait.

Operational signals & dashboards added
- New per-mini-slot metrics emitted: slot_fill_pct, avg_wait_ms, kv_affinity_hits, slot_age_ms, prefill_evictions.
- Dashboards: per-model mini-slot heatmaps, tail-latency waterfall by slot-size, retry-train detector alert.

Actionable recommendations (near-term)
1) Roll out Run A config to canary (10% of hostpool, routing policy: route-only-low-latency-apps) for 48h. (PR merged: see linked PR).
2) Add age-based demotion: if slot_age_ms > 25ms and fill_pct < 50% -> flush to avoid starving short requests.
3) Implement retry-train detector and short-circuit: if >3 identical signatures in 500ms within same queue -> bypass affinity wait for next 50ms.
4) Keep mini_slot_size <= 8 for PLG-facing routes; experiments show diminishing returns and tail regressions beyond that.

Longer-term
- Explore workload-aware dynamic sizing: adapt mini_slot_size by short-term estimated request size distribution. Consider tiny ML model in scheduler that predicts affinity arrivals (very small compute, e.g., single-layer LSTM/linear).
- Evaluate interaction with batching on multi-instance pinned kernels (when multiple concurrent instances compete for CUDA streams) — currently untested.
- Consider making affinity_window_ms derived from KV cache TTL and model decode step count rather than fixed ms.

Open questions / unknowns
- Edge-case behavior when KV cache state is partially stale (stale entries cause subtle output differences). Need to confirm that affinity grouping never violates freshness semantics for pinned-private caches.
- Does affinity grouping cause uneven wear on cache eviction patterns on multi-tenant pools? We saw slight skew; need longer runs with production traffic.

Next experiments (planned)
- Canary step with Run A config, collect 7d traces and run offline analysis comparing rollout routes vs control on p999 and fairness index.
- Short A/B: Run B config on 5% of traffic to verify fairness profile for internal/automation routes.
- Test interaction with quantized kernels (int8) and half-precision decode paths — microbench additional runs to ensure no kernel launch regression.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally iterative: lots of small heuristics here. Focus review on: (1) failure modes and mitigations (retry-train short-circuit) (2) performance counters emitted and naming (we should avoid overly chatty metrics) (3) config defaults: do we expose prefill_threshold_pct to customers or keep internal?

Appendix: quick numbers (selected)
- Baseline trace (2025-10-12): p50=19ms, p95=48ms, p99=220ms, p999=420ms, KV_hit=48%, gpu_util=72%
- Run A (best candidate): p50=18ms, p95=42ms, p99=160ms, p999=280ms, KV_hit=61%, gpu_util=69%
- Run B (low-latency focused): p50=20ms, p95=46ms, p99=210ms, p999=400ms, KV_hit=53%, gpu_util=74%
- Run C (large slot): p50=21ms, p95=58ms, p99=310ms, p999=520ms, KV_hit=70%, gpu_util=64%

Action items (owners)
- Priya: prepare canary rollout plan + update runbook (due 2025-11-20).
- Evan: implement retry-train detector in scheduler (PR draft: /serving-runtime#987) (due 2025-11-14).
- Marta: run 7d traffic replay subset and produce fairness report (due 2025-11-26).

-- end of notes (rough).
